gen-dafont-neon-gf-noto-sans-gothic: Noto Sans Gothic has big, round-bellied lowercase with counters like drilled glass beads, a plain sans through and through. Neon's glowing, hairline-free strokes sit above it, and the two keep each other lit.
gen-dafont-neon-gf-noto-sans-grantha: Neon draws every letter as a bent paperclip, one uniform line with no thick-thin shifts. Noto Sans Grantha does the opposite job, with tall little letters that read smoothly because no bowl ever closes up.
gen-dafont-neon-gf-noto-sans-gujarati: Wire-like and glowing, Neon glides under the eye in one unbroken line width. Noto Sans Gujarati follows in sans-serif form, its curved strokes stopping short of turning inward and leaving large open counters.
gen-dafont-neon-gf-noto-sans-gunjala-gon: Neon cuts every letter at a single depth, like an engraver who never pressed harder in places, glowing and vibrant. And Noto Sans Gunjala Gondi brings sans-serif lowercase as tall as a thick crayon mark, with terminals cut back to leave big gaps.
gen-dafont-neon-gf-noto-sans-gurmukhi: Neon holds a pencil-line consistency from start to finish. Noto Sans Gurmukhi adds outward-pointing terminals like tongs and ascenders that barely clear the x-height, giving the glow of the heading a clean, tidy partner.
gen-dafont-neon-gf-noto-sans-hanunoo: Vibrant and glowing, Neon draws its letters with a ballpoint's pressure-free line, nothing thick or thin anywhere. Noto Sans Hanunoo fills most of its height with lowercase and keeps its terminals open.
gen-dafont-neon-gf-noto-sans-hebrew: Glowing tubes of letters, tall and stamped. Neon is best at holding one untapered line, as a quill never would, while Noto Sans Hebrew is best at its dominant midsection and wide gaps between curve ends and stems.
gen-dafont-neon-gf-noto-sans-hk: Twine pressed into a flat surface: that is Neon, glowing and vibrant, with open spacing between every pair of letters. Noto Sans HK has large lowercase and tight ascenders, so give that body the smaller size.
gen-dafont-neon-gf-noto-sans-imperial-ar: Noto Sans Imperial Aramaic reads approachably, its c ends pointing apart like open pincers and capitals sitting a short step above the lowercase. Neon does glow best, a thick-only outline from end to end, while the body quietly carries the text.
gen-dafont-neon-gf-noto-sans-inscription: Neon's letters look like bent tubing, glowing and uniform. Noto Sans Inscriptional Parthian has big open eyes in every e and a and a deep middle band, so a longer passage would flow smoothly and without strain.
